clue.text: A dull Common Market leader in Rome — one with superficial understanding

parts.note: matt or mat describes a finish without shine
the EU grew out of the European Common Market

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Rome

explanation.surface: A dreary Brussels figure heading to Rome is mocked as a mere dabbler in the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler or non-professional often has only a shallow grasp of a field, which is this sense of the word.

clue.text: Great — it lasts for 31 days

definitions.meaning: the eighth month of the year has 31 days

explanation.surface: Something wonderful lasts a whole month.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means majestic or eminent; the capitalised noun is the summer month with 31 days.

clue.text: It's said Victoria wasn't so considered to support Albert at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up
at first takes the opening letter of Albert

parts.note: mused means considered or pondered

explanation.surface: The Queen pondered whether to back her consort Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously quoted as saying 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation attributed to Victoria denies being entertained, so the definition describes that state.

clue.text: Digital TV one cleric ordered, but no volume

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order
but no means except for, so the letter for volume is dropped from the TV

explanation.surface: A churchman orders a digital television set.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop V from TV to leave T, then 'ordered' rearranges T + ONE CLERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital devices are those operating by electronic circuitry rather than mechanically.

clue.text: Intensely heat pan

definitions.meaning: to cook meat in an oven at high heat
to pan is to criticise harshly, as in a review

explanation.surface: Instructions to heat a cooking pan fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking in a hot oven is one sense; a savage review or tearing a performance apart is the other.

clue.text: Attacked at home — very cheesed off, scratching head

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: scratching out the head of the word removes its first letter

parts.note: cheesed off is British slang for fed up, which is jaded

explanation.surface: A householder, fed up after a burglary, complains of being attacked while at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheesed off' is British slang for weary or fed up, i.e. JADED; 'scratching head' drops its J to leave ADED.
explanation.definitionFit: To invade is to enter by force, so the past tense matches having been attacked.

clue.text: Bury hamster, maybe keeping right shed light on

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the pet word surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: a hamster is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Burying a pet hamster, perhaps with the rites done properly, explains everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to explain it, making its meaning clear.

clue.text: Cover your sandwiches thoroughly

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: An instruction to wrap your sandwiches carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Very and thoroughly are both intensifiers meaning completely, as in the very end.

clue.text: Doctor on violin about to be sensational

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: an Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona
c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A physician playing a violin is set to be a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic means striking or spectacular, a synonym for sensational.

clue.text: Imagining what those who have retired might be doing

definitions.meaning: fancying or picturing in the mind

definitions.text: what those who have retired might be doing
definitions.meaning: retired here means gone to bed, where they would be asleep and having visions

explanation.surface: Pondering what pensioners get up to all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasising is daydreaming; sleepers also experience visions in the night.

clue.text: Look around centre of Rouen for thin fabric

indicators.note: the word for look goes around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: the centre of the five-letter Rouen is its third letter

explanation.surface: A tourist in Rouen browses the shops looking for some light, sheer material.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is a sheer, loosely woven textile, used for bandages and veils.

clue.text: A large bird had food every second

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a tern is a seabird
ate is the past tense of eat, to have food

explanation.surface: A big seabird apparently ate food at every moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second' looks like a time phrase, but it is the definition: as in 'on alternate days'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on alternate days happens on every other, or every second, one.

clue.text: They watch top actress working

indicators.note: working means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading actress is on stage while the audience looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators are onlookers, people who watch an event.

clue.text: Heated conflict with male

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: A furious battle involving a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated is a synonym for raised in temperature, as in a heated room.

clue.text: Insect flutters if one gets caught how biologist's described?

indicators.note: an insect that flutters moves about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bug flits about until it is trapped; how would a naturalist describe it?
explanation.definitionFit: A biologist is a scientist, so their work is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Making prisoners upset in court? About time

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shuffled letters surround the abbreviation for time
upset means knocked over and rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Convicts are distressed in a courtroom about how long they will serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' shuffles IN COURT into INCOURT's arrangement TRUCION, and 'About' wraps it round T to give TRUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Construction is the act of building or creating, so it equals making.

clue.text: Corset plus buckles — everything initially removed for artists

indicators.note: buckles means bends out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
removed means that letter is taken out of the word Corset
initially takes the first letter of everything

explanation.surface: Corsets and buckles are taken off entirely, as for a life-drawing class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially removed' takes the E from CORSET, leaving CORST; 'buckles' rearranges CORST + PLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculptors are artists who carve or model three-dimensional works.

clue.text: State-of-the-art vehicle — church splitting total

indicators.note: splitting means breaking apart, so the other pieces go inside the word for total

parts.note: to add is to total
a van is a vehicle
CE is short for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cutting-edge vehicle, with the church dividing the overall amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced technology is modern, at the leading edge of development.

clue.text: Authorised chemical company once to get in waste material

indicators.note: get in means enter, so the company's initials go inside the other word

parts.note: offal can mean refuse or waste matter
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British chemicals firm

explanation.surface: An approved former chemicals firm manages to get rid of its waste.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI (Imperial Chemical Industries) was a large British chemicals company, broken up in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Official means approved by those in authority, synonymous with authorised.

clue.text: Problems beginning to double — if female is embracing religious sect, that is

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from double
embracing means holding inside, so the word is goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Trouble mounts as a woman joins a fringe religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps IS round the sect and the Latin abbreviation, so the closing S of the answer comes from IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficulties are troubles or obstacles, a plural synonym of problems.

clue.text: Find old animal let outside with no tail

indicators.note: outside means the shortened word goes around the other pieces
with no tail means the last letter of let is cut off

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Tracking down an elderly pet that was allowed out, minus its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' cuts LET to LE, which goes round OCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is, i.e. to find it.

clue.text: Expect half to leave after snake's appearance

indicators.note: after means the remainder follows the snake word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: half to leave means the first three of the six letters of Expect go

explanation.surface: Anticipate half of them to go once the snake shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half to leave' removes the first three of Expect's six letters; 'appearance' means look or outlook here.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect means the look or appearance of something, as in a gloomy aspect.

clue.text: Greedy, temperamental woman coming over

indicators.note: coming over means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a temperamental female star

explanation.surface: A grasping, moody woman is paying a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns DIVA back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, and can mean greedy, as in avid for gain.

clue.text: Actor is open about losing 100 jobs in the theatre?

indicators.note: about signals the letters moving around into a new order
losing means the letter for a hundred is dropped from the word Actor

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A performer frets about a hundred jobs being cut at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C from ACTOR to leave ATOR, and 'about' shuffles ATOR with IS OPEN. The theatre here is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeries carried out in an operating theatre are the jobs done there.

clue.text: It's used to spy planes going up and down

indicators.note: going up and down means the word reads the same both ways in a down light

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A device for detecting aircraft flying up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up and down' describes the planes, but it says the word reads identically in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar detects aircraft by bouncing radio waves off them.

clue.text: Fancy a fish for starters?

indicators.note: for starters means the fish is served first, so it moves in front of the letter before it

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A question of whether to order fish as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, which is a synonym for a thought or concept.

clue.text: Term for minors?

parts.note: the term is a period of time, not a word: the span of years when one is a minor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' reads as a word or name, but it means a stretch of time, the years spent as a minor.
explanation.definitionFit: The years before adulthood are the period during which a person is a minor.

clue.text: Set up game of snooker?

definitions.meaning: to set someone up is to incriminate them falsely
a single game in snooker is called a ...

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a game of snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: To incriminate falsely is to set up; a snooker match is played as a series of individual games of that name.

clue.text: Diana perhaps hugging everyone in return for money

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the surname surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Diana Dors was a British film actress of the 1950s

indicators.note: in return means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Diana embraces everybody in exchange for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Dors was a famous British film star of the 1950s. 'in return' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollars are the currency of the USA and elsewhere, so a word for money.

clue.text: In Germany, I, among others, should be most wealthy

indicators.note: among means set in the midst of, so the German word sits inside the other piece

parts.note: the rest means the others
ich is German for I

explanation.surface: A German claims that he, with his peers, ought to be the wealthiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Richest is the superlative of rich, meaning wealthiest.
